newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition to raise oil prices, official says.
newsitem.headline: India coalition to raise oil prices, official says.

text.p: India's ruling coalition will soon raise domestic oil prices to curb a mounting subsidy bill, a senior alliance official said on Wednesday.

"There is no option but to increase prices which we would do shortly," the official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters after the United Front coalition postponed a decision on oil prices for the fourth time in three months.
Earlier on Wednesday, the 15-party coalition failed at a 30-minute meeting to decide on whether to increase the prices of some petroleum products to curtail the escalating cost of consumer subsidies.
At the end of March, the government owed $4.3 billion to state oil firms, which sell some products like kerosene to consumers at prices that are below international levels.

The coalition's decision-making Steering Committee has met four times since May to consider proposals to raise prices, but leftwing alliance partners including communists have voiced strong opposition, saying a price increase would hurt the poor.
Information Minister Jaipal Reddy said the coalition would meet again soon to take up the issue.
